title: Field operator signal docket — wildcard plays
content:
Purpose
Short working ledger of customer-facing runtime problems observed in the field (last 60d) + pragmatic wildcard plays (cheap operator/console knobs and small-engineering patches) we can surface to customers or ship quickly. Focus: stopgap mitigations that reduce customer toil and incident volume while product/infra designs mature.

Context / how to use this doc
- Designed for CS responders, solutions engineers, on-call infra/ops.
- Not a final roadmap — these are lightweight plays: config toggles, route guards, rate-limiter templates, and small server-side patches.
- Each item includes: symptom vignette, quick play (what to do now), why it helps, rough effort and risk.

Quick signals (high-level themes)
- KV cache warming volatility: customers hit tail latency spikes when long-running chat sessions touch cold KV shards after autoscaling events.
- Embedding batch failures: intermittent E2E 500s when the batching window collides with large requests and memory pressure on dedicated pools.
- Tokenization drift: third-party tokenizers produce a token-count mismatch vs our estimator leading to runaway billing surprises for a subset of customers using non-standard text pre-processing.
- Silent streaming disconnects: streaming clients (websocket + SSE clients via SDK) see connection completes w/o final chunk; user sees truncated responses.
- Rerank flakiness under load: reranking jobs degrade quality when fallbacks to lower-context variants are triggered automatically.

Representative vignettes (raw field notes)
1) Small fintech customer, multi-stage chatflows. Symptom: occasional 800–1200ms token-latency spikes for certain user journeys after a short incident; customers see slowness on otherwise stable SLA. Observed: cold KV-cache after node replacement; autoscaler rebalanced pods across pools.
2) Marketplace customer doing bulk-embed refreshes (20k items) — bursts cause transient 502s from embedding node pool. Workaround: serializing the batch helped, but cost/latency skyrocketed.
3) Internal partner using a custom pre-tokenizer: they reported token accounting mismatch (our cost estimate vs actual billed tokens). Caused surprised discounts/rebates requests.
4) SaaS customer using streaming on a flaky mobile network: final message chunk consistently missing when client uses resumable reconnects in the SDK.

Wildcard plays (prioritized)
- Play A: Warm-before-serve toggle (operator) — Very low effort (ops config change).
  - What: Add a per-route option in console to pre-warm KV shards for active sessions (simple: trigger a light prefix replay to prime caches when a session is created or resumed).
  - Why: Avoids cold-KV tail spikes; non-invasive; reversible.
  - Risk: CPU/RTX overhead small if rate-limited.
  - Owner: ops -> Lina.

- Play B: Embedding-window-sizer guard (engineer + ops) — Small patch (2–3 days dev, 1 day rollout).
  - What: Introduce a soft-limit for auto-batched embedding requests; if payload > threshold, split into bounded windows and use backpressure metrics instead of throwing 502. Add helpful 429 with retry-after for customer SDKs.
  - Why: Reduces memory pressure; clearer failure semantics.
  - Risk: Slightly higher average latency for oversized batches but far fewer hard failures.
  - Owner: eng-applied-ml -> Jonah.

- Play C: Token-count calibration endpoint (product + docs) — Minimal engineer time + docs update.
  - What: Provide a console endpoint that runs customer's snippet through the exact tokenizer pipeline used for billing and returns the estimate. Expose a small SDK helper.
  - Why: Lowers customer surprise, reduces billing disputes.
  - Risk: None; data isolated.
  - Owner: devexp -> Ravi.

- Play D: Streaming final-chunk ack (quick SDK patch) — 1–2 day SDK change + hotfix.
  - What: Add explicit final-chunk sentinel and client-side backoff/retry that requests the last chunk if missing; server side emits a final ack event.
  - Why: Robust to flaky networks; easy workaround for mobile clients.
  - Risk: Breaking if clients assume different framing; include compatibility flag.
  - Owner: devexp -> SDK leads.

- Play E: Rerank-fallback transparency flag (console + runtime) — small product + runtime change.
  - What: Expose a per-route boolean: "prefer-quality-over-latency". When true, do not degrade to lower-context reranker variants; instead queue or return a soft degrade message.
  - Why: Gives customers control to avoid silent quality regressions in high-value flows.
  - Risk: Could increase p99 latency; must be gated behind quota/alerts.
  - Owner: product-hosted-api.

Triage matrix (impact -> effort shorthand)
- Quick wins (impact high, effort small): Warm-before-serve toggle; Token-count calibration endpoint; Streaming final-chunk ack.
- Medium bets (impact medium, effort medium): Embedding-window-sizer guard; Rerank-fallback transparency flag.
- Longer runway (impact high, effort high): Smart KV sharding by conversational affinity; autoscaler-aware prefetching algorithm (needs infra investment).

Notes to engineering (implementation hints)
- For warm-before-serve: implement a lightweight prefix hook that replays the last 2–4 user messages into cache; make it throttled (per-customer concurrency cap) and visible in console metrics.
- For embedding windows: prefer deterministic chunking that preserves ordering; add a per-chunk trace id so diagnostics can stitch partial results. Return an error summary that references the chunk id.
- Token calibration: reuse the billing token pipeline (exact same tokenizer + model-specific byte handling). Add an "explain" mode that returns token-breakdown.
- Streaming ack: add short TTL ack events so SDKs can request missing final-chunk within that TTL. Avoid re-sending full payloads; server should stream only the diff or final tail.

Communications draft (for CS replies)
- When customers report tail latency: apologize, explain warm-before-serve pilot, offer to enable on affected routes ("We can enable a pre-warm toggle scoped to X routes for 48h to validate"). Offer diagnostics: attach per-request kv-warm metrics and p50/p95 token latency.
- For embedding 502s: advise immediate workaround: chunk on client side using batch_size <= 200 (or concrete threshold per customer's median vector size) and enable retry-with-backoff. Commit to a roadmap item and share ETA.
- For tokenization gap: provide token-calibration link and propose a short sync to confirm pre-processing. Offer to run customer's sample through our billing pipeline.

Open questions & blockers
- Telemetry: do we have per-route KV-warm hit-rate and shard-level tail metrics surfaced in console? If not, ops needs a simple dashboard.
- Quota semantics: enabling warm-before-serve will increase short-term token counts — how to surface to customers so they don't assume misuse? Need a console note and a small credit policy for trials.
- SDK compatibility for streaming-ack sentinel: how to roll without breaking older clients? Suggest a graceful feature-negotiation header.

Next steps (action items)
- Lina: prototype the operator toggle and a small dashboard tile showing warm hits by route — due 2027-06-22.
- Jonah: spike embedding-window-sizer to validate chunking strategy and failure semantics — due 2027-06-18.
- Ravi: assemble a token-calibration endpoint spec + sample SDK helper — due 2027-06-17.
- CS (Ava): run this playbook with three impacted customers this week as trial and capture outcome notes in the sheet linked below.

Appendix: quick play scripts (ops cheats)
- Console command to enable per-route pre-warm: (ops only) enable-route-prefetch --route <ROUTE_ID> --prefix-window 3 --rate-limit 5/s
- Temporary embedding chunk policy (recommended): add header X-Embed-Window: 512 and treat as opt-in when customers explicitly set it.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep record of customer outcomes in the trial sheet: link to CS trial sheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1-field-trial-sample (internal).
- Revisit after 30d: measure incident volume delta, p99 latency delta for warmed routes, and customer satisfaction (CSAT) on the three trial accounts.

End of working docket.

(Informal — expect fragments, shorthand, and followups in comments.)
